name: S01 isOrdered: a region whose start is after its end is allowed
why: the lookup takes the binary search over arrays like 0..1, 10..3, 5..20 (the starts out of order) and answers 7 false where the oracle says true

name: S02 isOrdered: the chain test is dropped
why: unsorted, overlapping and nested arrays are searched by their starts: 0..10 then 3..4 answers 6 false where the oracle says true

name: S03 isOrdered: a region may start at the line the previous one ends
why: EQUIVALENT in the answer: in a touching pair (end of one = start of the next) the last start at or below a line L is the second region exactly when L is at or above the shared line, which both regions hold, so the search finds a region that holds L whenever one does (argued, and no row disagrees: the named row of regions that touch at a line, E1's touching pairs over the pool and the seeded arrays with a touching pair all agree under it)

name: S04 isOrdered: the chain test is reversed
why: ordered arrays are refused (a slow pass, the same answer) and overlapping ones are accepted (a wrong answer)

name: S05 isOrdered: the guard on the first region is dropped
why: the first region is compared with the NaN that starts previousEnd, so every array is refused and every ask is a pass over every region: the same answers, slow (killed by the read-count and clock rows, not by an answer)

name: S06 isOrdered: previousEnd starts at minus infinity
why: EQUIVALENT: the first region's comparison is guarded by `i > 0`, so the starting value is never read

name: S07 isOrdered: the end says no
why: every array is refused: the same answers, slow (killed by the read-count and clock rows)

name: S08 isOrdered: previousEnd is never updated
why: previousEnd stays NaN, so every array of two regions or more is refused: the same answers, slow (killed by the read-count and clock rows)

name: S09 lookup: the ordered and the unordered swap their answers
why: an unordered array is searched by its starts and answered wrongly

name: S10 lookup: always the pass over every region
why: the seam again: the same answers, slow (killed by the read-count and clock rows)

name: S11 lookup: never the pass over every region
why: an unordered array is searched by its starts and answered wrongly

name: S12 lookup: the order is checked at every ask
why: the same answers, a pass over every region at every ask: killed by the read-count and clock rows

name: S13 lookup: the fallback answers false
why: an unordered array holds nothing

name: S14 search: the low end starts at the second region
why: the first region is never found

name: S15 search: the high end stops before the last region
why: the last region is never found

name: S16 search: nothing found starts at the first region
why: a line above the first region is compared with the first region's end, and an empty array reads regions[0]

name: S17 search: the loop stops with one candidate left
why: a one-region array is never searched

name: S18 search: the middle is the high end
why: a downward walk from the last region: the same answers, a pass over every region (killed by the read-count and clock rows)

name: S19 search: the middle by an unsigned shift
why: EQUIVALENT: high - low is never negative inside the loop, and an array has fewer than 2^31 regions

name: S20 search: a start is strictly below the line
why: a line on a region's first line is not found

name: S21 search: the low end skips a region
why: a region right after a candidate is skipped

name: S22 search: the high end skips a region
why: a region right before a candidate is skipped

name: S23 search: the end is exclusive
why: a region's last line is outside it

name: S24 search: no check that anything was found
why: a line above the first region reads regions[-1]

name: S25 search: found is tested with >= 0
why: EQUIVALENT: found is -1 or an index

name: S26 search: the start is compared where the end should be
why: only a region's first line is inside it

name: S27 isOrdered: a NaN start is allowed
why: a NaN bound passes the first test; [NaN..1, 2..2] is then searched by its starts, the NaN start is never at or below a line, and 2 is answered false where the oracle says true (killed by E1)

name: S28 isOrdered: the chain test says >= for the negation
why: EQUIVALENT: `!(a < b)` and `a >= b` differ only for a NaN, and a NaN bound has already failed the start-before-end test of its own region (a NaN end fails it for that region, a NaN start for that one)

name: W01 collectValueSources: the filter keeps the option lines IN a region
why: the cells inside a region are kept and the others dropped

name: W02 collectValueSources: the filter asks about the option line, not the fence
why: EQUIVALENT in the answer: an option line is a `#|` line directly under its cell's fence, and a region's delimiters are `---` lines, so no delimiter lies between a fence and any of its option lines and both are on the same side of every region: asking about the option line is the same question

name: W03 collectValueSources: the lookup is made at every ask
to:
const regions = quartoYamlRegions(text);
  const inYamlRegion = (line: number): boolean => createYamlRegionLookup(regions)(line);
why: the order is checked at every ask: the same answers, regions times option lines again (killed by the wiring row, which counts 150 lookups for 150 option lines, and by the end-to-end clock rows)

name: W04 collectValueSources: the old spelling
to:
const regions = quartoYamlRegions(text);
  const inYamlRegion = (line: number): boolean => regions.some((r) => line >= r.startLine && line <= r.endLine);
why: the parent again: the same answers, regions times option lines (killed by the wiring row, which counts no lookup at all, and by the end-to-end clock rows)

name: W05 collectValueSources: two lookups are made
why: the same answers and twice the work of making the lookup: killed by the wiring rows, which count one lookup a call (the clock rows cannot see a constant factor of two on the cheap part)

name: T09 rows: the ratio limit is not strict

name: T10 rows: a run read as 0 is allowed

name: T11 rows: the counting wrapper counts nothing

name: T12 rows: the wrapper counts no lookup
